questions.title: DISTINCT Author Output
questions.description: Ten book rows reference six distinct authors. What does this query return?
questions.Option1: Six rows — each author at most once
questions.Option2: Authors sorted by how many books they wrote
questions.Option3: Only authors who wrote exactly one book
questions.codesnippet: SELECT DISTINCT author FROM books ORDER BY author;

questions.title: Rows Without ORDER BY
questions.description: A SELECT runs without an ORDER BY clause. In what order do the rows come back?
questions.Option3: No guaranteed order — only ORDER BY gives a guaranteed one

questions.title: Catalog Query Result

questions.title: DISTINCT Two Columns
questions.description: What does this query deduplicate over?
questions.Option2: The combination of author and pages
questions.Option4: Nothing — DISTINCT is ignored with two columns
questions.codesnippet: SELECT DISTINCT author, pages FROM books ORDER BY author;

questions.title: Why Alias Output Columns
questions.description: Well-behaved clients alias every output column because…
questions.Option1: Aliases make the query run faster
questions.Option3: Aliases encrypt the data in transit
questions.Option4: Aliased names make the result schema explicit and stable

questions.title: Bag Semantics of Results
questions.description: Without DISTINCT, a relational query result is best described as…
questions.Option1: An ordered list with unique rows
questions.Option2: A bag (multiset) of rows — duplicates possible, order not guaranteed

questions.title: Tie-Break Ordering
questions.description: Two books both have 176 pages. How does this query order them relative to each other?
questions.Option1: By title ascending — the second key breaks the tie
questions.Option4: It errors — ORDER BY cannot handle ties
questions.codesnippet: SELECT title, pages FROM books ORDER BY pages DESC, title ASC;
